title: Coordinate naturality and canonical punctured-line exchange after relative calculation
statement: For a purity finite setting P, divisibility h, arbitrary k-schemes Y and Y prime, a structure map a on Y and a morphism g : Y prime to Y, assume RelativeKummerConclusions of [def-pur-relative-kummer-maps] on both bases. Then pullback of coordinateClass is coordinateClass on the new base under the specified coefficient and shift identifications, and the specified canonical punctured-line derived exchange is an isomorphism. coordinateClass is the actual coordinateKummer morphism with reflexive coefficient-complex equality maps. This result assumes the relative calculations; it proves no relative calculation and includes no affine-line exchange assertion.

proof.text: Pull back the exact Kummer sequence and use pullback of units on its middle and right terms and canonical root-line pullback on its left term. Naturality of the connecting morphism, followed by coefficient insertion, proves naturality of the actual coordinate boundary. Exact single-complex comparison and the reflexive coefficient identifications give precisely the displayed coordinateClass equality.

The exchange is the adjunction mate of the inverse-image square. The mate-unit identity shows that its composite with pullback of the unit is the new unit, under the canonical coefficient identifications. Thus its degree-zero map preserves constants and is an isomorphism by the assumed relative degree-zero calculations.

Forget module coefficients using the canonical exchange comparison. On injective resolutions, cohomology of the exchange is the map obtained by termwise underived exchange and a resolution comparison. The representative-section formula restricts a cocycle to the base-changed etale object. Etale restriction preserves the resolutions used here. The naturality of the actual boundary from the first step therefore identifies its action on the actual degree-one Kummer edge section with the new coordinate section. The assumed generator isomorphisms on the two bases make this degree-one map an isomorphism.

Exact inverse image commutes with cohomology. The assumed punctured-line calculations kill both sides in positive degrees above one; right-derived left exactness kills negative degrees. The preceding two steps prove isomorphisms in the remaining degrees. Cohomological detection of derived isomorphisms gives the punctured-line exchange isomorphism.

The punctured projections are affine and remain qcqs after arbitrary base change. Exact comparison, the specified invertible counit mates, and the canonical transport-identifies-exchange equation identify the etale exchange with the stated pro-etale exchange. The compared coordinate class is the published coordinateClass. The construction applies to every k-morphism, including geometric points.
